story.story_sentence: Hurricane Milton didn’t stop at the coast. The day after landfall, the Gulf-coast grid was drawing 0.89× its normal for a week, and 45% of it on the worst day, while 51 regions the storm missed did not move.
story.conversation_hook: The rest of the country didn’t budge. That is the whole trick: the test is Florida against 51 places the storm missed, then 1,646 fake dates.

effects.title: Duke Energy Florida electricity demand
effects.unit: its normal, the week after landfall
effects.headline: Duke Energy Florida demand, 0.89× its normal for the week after landfall
effects.plain: Duke Energy Florida, the utility for the Gulf coast where Milton came ashore, drew 0.89× its normal for the week from 10 Oct 2024. On 10 Oct 2024, the day after landfall, it drew 45% of normal. Together with Florida Power & Light the two grids ran 20% below 51 regions the storm never touched.

sources.text: 1 of 1 channels agree (EIA-930 hourly demand, physical channel); no attention or economic channel was registered for this series

mechanism.step: Wind and flooding knock out power to millions of customers
mechanism.why: Demand that cannot be served is not recorded as demand.

mechanism.step: Businesses and homes that still have power go dark or empty
mechanism.why: Evacuations and closures cut load even where lines hold.

mechanism.step: Demand climbs back as crews restore lines
mechanism.why: The series returns toward its band over the following two weeks.

effects.how: The engine compared the seven days from 10 Oct 2024 with the series' own robust normal (T 3.86), then re-ran the test on 1,646 fake dates for the same series: 3 came out this strong (about 1 in 412). On 49 other series at the real date, none did (1 in 50). Separately, the regional contrast put Florida's two grids against 51 unaffected regions and 41 pseudo-storms: none came close.
effects.mind: A reporting gap at the utility on those days, or a cold snap that hit Florida but not the donor regions, would make us re-check the size. Pre-trends were flat (p 0.42) and a synthetic control agrees in sign. The independent forecast model has not evaluated this series yet; until it does, the published word is Likely.

fluke.text: About 1 in 412 fake dates produce a move this big.

replication.rule: seen = the pre-registered regional contrast passed (in-space p <= 0.05, pre-trends flat, expected sign); the single-event 6.1 test has no replication record for this hop

family.note: Across the 27 past storms tested (24 once overlapping storms are merged) the pooled effect is null; most storms are mapped to whole grid operators (MISO, PJM) where a landfall is a rounding error. Milton and Ian, both mapped to Florida utilities, are the two that pass.

band.note: band = ±1.28σ, σ = current robust scale of the series (the engine’s own band for this series)

shore.title: New-business applications in hit states
shore.headline: Where hurricanes usually reach: fewer new businesses, four weeks on
shore.plain: Across 23 past hurricanes, applications to start a business in the hit states ran 3.2% below unaffected states over the following four weeks. Nobody pre-registered this for Milton, so Milton itself is untested on it: this is a rule about storms like it, not evidence about this storm.
